  def self.truncate(str, limit)
    return str if str.chars.count <= limit

    # Get the first limit characters of the original string
    # We need to handle multi-byte characters properly
    # str[0...limit] might split a character, so we need to be careful
    
    # Take characters one by one until we reach limit
    truncated = ""

        break
      end
      truncated << char

    if truncated.length == str.chars.count

    # Replace the last character(s) with ellipsis to make exactly limit characters

    truncated = truncated[0...-1] + "…"
    
    truncated
  end

  attr_reader :value

  def initialize
    @value = 0
    @step = 1
  end

  def bump
    @value += @step
    self
  end

  def with_step(step)
    old_step = @step
    begin
      @step = step
      yield self
    ensure

    end

    copy
  end

    copy = super
    copy.instance_variable_set(:@value, @value)
    copy.instance_variable_set(:@step, @step)
    copy
  end
end

  def initialize(from)
    @from = from
  end

  def each
    if block_given?
      @from.downto(1) { |i| yield i }
      self
    else
      StepsEnumerator.new(@from)

  class StepsEnumerator
    def initialize(from)
      @current = from
      @index = 0

    def next
      raise StopIteration if @current < 1
      result = @current
      @current -= 1
      @index += 1

  def self.parse(line)
    result = {}

    end
    
    result
  end
